title: From Synthetic Priors to Model Behavior: Structural Coverage in Tabular Foundation Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.06912v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are commonly pretrained on large collections of procedurally generated synthetic tasks, yet it remains unclear how well these synthetic pretraining priors support the downstream tasks on which the models are evaluated. We study this question from a distribution-level attribution perspective. We recover or reconstruct the synthetic data generators of four TFMs and compare their generated tasks with datasets from two widely used tabular benchmarks. Each dataset is represented by a common set of structural descriptors capturing schema, feature distributions, dependence structure, response properties, and feature--response relationships. In this space, we measure how broadly and repeatedly each synthetic prior reaches benchmark tasks using structural coverage and normalized density, and examine whether stronger local support is associated with better predictive performance. translated_title: 从合成先验到模型行为：表格基础模型中的结构覆盖度
translated_abstract: 表格基础模型（TFMs）通常在大量程序化生成的合成任务集合上进行预训练，然而这些合成预训练先验对模型所评估的下游任务的支持程度仍不清楚。我们从分布层面的归因视角来研究这一问题。我们恢复或重构了四个表格基础模型的合成数据生成器，并将其生成的任务与两个广泛使用的表格基准数据集进行比较。每个数据集都由一组共同的结构描述符表示，这些描述符涵盖模式、特征分布、依赖结构、响应属性以及特征-响应关系。在该空间中，我们使用结构覆盖度和归一化密度来衡量每个合成先验到达基准任务的广度与重复程度，并检验更强的局部支持是否与更好的预测性能相关联。我们发现存在显著差异……（原文摘要至此被截断）
tldr: 该论文从分布层面归因视角出发，通过结构覆盖度和归一化密度量化表格基础模型的合成预训练先验对下游基准任务的支持范围，并探究这种结构支持与预测性能之间的关联。
en_tdlr: This paper takes a distribution-level attribution perspective to quantify how well the synthetic pretraining priors of tabular foundation models reach downstream benchmark tasks, using structural coverage and normalized density, and examines whether stronger local structural support correlates with better predictive performance.
